question: What was the score of India in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for 2024 released by Transparency International in February 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**38**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2024** was released by the global civil society organization **Transparency International** in **February 2025**.
 
• **India** recorded a score of **38** out of **100** in the **2024** index, reflecting the perceived level of public sector corruption in the country.
 
• In comparison to the **2023** report, where India scored **39**, the current score of **38** indicates a slight decline in the perceived integrity of the public sector.
 
• India’s rank in the **2024** index is **93rd** among **180 countries** and territories evaluated globally.
 
• The index uses a scale where **0** represents "highly corrupt" and **100** represents "very clean," placing India in the lower half of the global rankings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transparency International:**
 
 
• It is an international non-governmental organization based in **Berlin, Germany**, founded in **1993**.
 
• The organization aims to take action to combat global corruption and prevent criminal activities arising from corruption.
 
• It publishes various reports including the **Global Corruption Barometer** and the **Corruption Perceptions Index**.
 
 
 
• **Top Performers in 2024:**
 
 
• Countries like **Denmark**, **Finland**, and **New Zealand** consistently rank at the top of the index with scores above **85**.
 
• These nations are characterized by strong **rule of law**, independent **judicial systems**, and high levels of **transparency**.
 
 
 
• **Global Average:**
 
 
• The **global average score** for the CPI remains stagnant at **43** for several consecutive years, indicating that most countries are failing to tackle public sector corruption effectively.
 
• More than **two-thirds** of countries score below **50**, highlighting serious corruption issues worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CPI Methodology:**
 
 
• The index aggregates data from **13 external sources**, including the **World Bank**, the **World Economic Forum**, and private risk and consulting companies.
 
• It focuses specifically on **public sector corruption**, including bribery, diversion of public funds, and the use of public office for private gain.
 
 
 
• **Regional Context (South Asia):**
 
 
• Within **South Asia**, **India** (**38**) and **Maldives** (**39**) often share similar score ranges, while **Pakistan** and **Bangladesh** typically record significantly lower scores.
 
• The **2024** report emphasized that the decline in **justice system** independence is a key driver for lower scores in many democratic nations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Corruption:**
 
 
• A low score in the **Corruption Perceptions Index** can negatively impact a country's **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** and overall **economic growth**.
 
• Corruption is frequently linked to social inequality and the erosion of **democratic institutions**.
